summary: PDF pages 1-2 bridge adjacent sections: motivates selective communication by treating message bandwidth and information content as learnable resources; then defines the partially observable cooperative MARL setting and positions learned communication against prior protocols.

PDF pages 3-4 connects channel capacity to message entropy and derives the information objective used to regularize communication. Literal retrieval anchors include Proposition 1, Proposition 2, Proposition 3.

PDF pages 5-7 bridge adjacent sections: specifies IMAC's encoder, variational information bottleneck, critic integration, and optimization objective; then evaluates communication quality and task return in predator-prey and related settings under the reported training/evaluation protocol. Literal retrieval anchors include Algorithm 1.

PDF pages 8-9 bridge adjacent sections: evaluates communication quality and task return in predator-prey and related settings under the reported training/evaluation protocol; then summarizes the bandwidth-information tradeoff without claiming held-out-roster robustness.
PDF pages 10-11 lists learned-communication, information-bottleneck, and cooperative-MARL sources used by the paper.
